text:
Sara Kim: Quick UX question — for the 'Create Dataset' stepper, should field errors show inline on blur or only after submit? trying to balance noise vs guidance. Mike Chen: inline on blur for atomic fields (email, name) so users get early feedback. for big textareas, wait until submit or on explicit validation. Ana Rodrigues: Agree on blur for simple fields. important: screen readers must announce that error. use aria-live and focus management. Jason Patel: Also, do we keep the asterisk required marker or explicit 'Required' label? asterisk alone feels terse. Sara Kim: Asterisk + visually-hidden text for assistive tech sounds good. but on mobile we might show 'Required' inline under the label to reduce discovery issues. Ana Rodrigues: Example ARIA snippet I propose: ```html
Enter a valid email address.
``` Mike Chen: design-bot flagged contrast on current error red (#d32f2f) — fails 4.5:1 for body text. can UX pick an accessible red? design-bot: automated check: error label contrast 3.8:1; recommended >=4.5. Jason Patel: For destructive actions (delete dataset), should we do typed confirm (type dataset name) or a simple modal with checkbox + 'Delete' button? Sara Kim: Typed confirm is safest but heavy. maybe tiered: simple modal for small things, typed confirm for org-level or very large datasets. Ana Rodrigues: Could be rule-based: size > 1GB OR shared with >5 projects => require typed confirm. else modal with a required checkbox. Mike Chen: Also UX detail — when submit fails, keep user input intact (do not clear fields) and focus the first invalid field. highlight it and show concise copy. Sara Kim: Copy voice: short & clear. prefer: 'Enter a valid email address.' vs longer conversational lines. designers? Ana Rodrigues: Lean concise: 'Enter a valid email address.' Also avoid punctuation-heavy messages. Jason Patel: Quick nit: error icons need accessible names (aria-hidden true for decorative, or role="img" + alt when informative). Mike Chen: I'll mock up two flows: inline-on-blur + accessible error patterns, and submit-only with global summary. will annotate aria attributes. Sara Kim: Perfect — I'll add both to the Figma page and flag for an a11y pass. can @Ana and @Jason review after I upload? :thumbsup: Ana Rodrigues: Yep, will review. Jason Patel: On it. Sara Kim: thanks team — will follow up with mock images and copy options later today.
